n: The last of the seven traditional penitential psalms. David appeals not to his own merit but to God’s faithfulness and righteousness.
‘Don’t put me on trial, for no living person is righteous before you.’ Paul echoes this verse in teaching that we are saved by grace.

f.w: in thy sight shall no man living be justified

n: The enemy has hunted him, crushed him to the ground, and forced him into darkness like the long-dead.

f.w: as those that have been long dead

n: His spirit grows faint and his heart is numb with dismay.
He finds strength in remembering how God acted in the past. Pondering God’s works restores hope.

f.w: I remember the days of old

n: He reaches out his hands to God; his soul thirsts for him like dry, cracked ground thirsts for rain.
‘Answer me quickly; my spirit is failing. Don’t hide your face, or I’ll be like those going down to the grave.’

f.w: hide not thy face from me

n: ‘Let me hear your steadfast love in the morning; show me the way to walk.’ Each new day starts with seeking God’s guidance.

f.w: cause me to know the way

n: ‘Rescue me from my enemies; I run to you for shelter.’

f.w: I flee unto thee to hide me

n: A beautiful prayer: ‘Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Let your good Spirit lead me on level ground.’

f.w: Teach me to do thy will

f.g: Level ground — a smooth, safe path.

n: ‘Give me life for your name’s sake; bring me out of trouble because you are righteous.’
In his covenant love, may God silence the enemies, ‘for I am your servant.’ Belonging to God is the final ground of his plea.
